537:
Each consumer subscribing to use the water and sewer service of the city shall pay a meter installation and connection fee times the number of water connections desired for water service and a sewer tap fee times the number of connections desired for sewer service. A reconnection fee shall be paid when connecting to any existing sewer lines that are available. If the sewer service is disconnected for any reason an additional re-connect fee shall be paid. Such fees shall be as established from time to time by the city council and set forth in the schedule of fees and charges, available for examination at city hall. Before water and sewer service is made available to the consumer an inspection by a duly authorized agent for the city must be made.
(Ord. of 9-3-1991(3), § 3)
538:
The minimum charge, as provided in the rate schedule, shall be made for such connection subscribed for. Water furnished for a given lot shall be used on that lot only and, except for fire protection, the city shall not under any condition furnish water free of charge to anyone.
(Ord. of 9-3-1991(3), § 4)
539:
The city shall run a service line from its distribution line to the property line where the distribution line exists or is to be constructed, and runs immediately adjacent and parallel to the property to be served. No service charge, other than the connection fee referred to in section 32-243, will be made for a five-eighths-inch by three-fourths-inch meter. A proportionately greater charge than the connection fee in section 32-243 will be made for a meter of larger dimensions.
(1) The city may make connections to service other properties not adjacent to its lines upon payment of reasonable cost for the extensions of its distribution lines as may be required to render such service.
(2) The city may install its meter at or near the property line or, at the city's option, on the consumer's property within three feet of the property line.
(3) The city reserves the right to refuse service unless the consumer's lines or pipings are installed in such a manner as to prevent cross connections or backflow.
(4) Under normal conditions the consumer will be notified of any anticipated interruptions of service by the city.
(Ord. of 9-3-1991(3), § 5)
540:
Water furnished by the city shall be used for consumption by the consumer, members of his household and employees only. The consumer shall not sell water to any other person or permit any other person to use said water. Water shall not be used for irrigation, fire protection, or other purposes, except when water is available in sufficient quantity without interfering with the regular domestic consumption in the area served. Disregard for this rule shall be sufficient cause for refusal and/or discontinuance of service.
(1) Where a meter or meter box is placed on the premises of a consumer, a suitable place shall be provided by the consumer therefore, unobstructed and accessible at all times to the meter reader.
(2) The consumer shall furnish and maintain a private cutoff valve on the consumer's side of the meter.
(3) The consumer's piping and apparatus shall be installed and maintained by the consumer at the consumer's expense, and in a safe and efficient manner, and in accordance with the sanitary regulations of the state department of public health.
(4) In order to be received as a consumer and entitled to receive water from the city's water system, all applicants must offer proof that any private wells located on their property are not physically connected to the lines of the city's water system and all applicants, by becoming consumers of the city, covenant and agree that so long as they continue to be consumers of the city they will not permit the connection of any private wells on their property to the city's water system.
(Ord. of 9-3-1991(3), § 6)
541:
(a) Duly authorized agents of the city shall have access at all hours to the premises of the consumer for the purpose of installing or removing city property, inspecting piping, reading and testing meters, or for any other purpose in connection with the water service and its facilities, and the sewer service and its facilities.
(b) Extensions to the system shall be made only when the consumer shall grant or convey, or shall cause to be granted or conveyed, to the city a permanent easement of right-of-way across any property traversed by the water and sewer lines.
(Ord. of 9-3-1991(3), § 7)
542:
Not less than three days' notice must be given, in person or in writing, at city hall to discontinue water and sewer service or to change occupancy. The outgoing party shall be responsible for all water consumed up to the time of departure or the time specified for departure, whichever period is longer. The new occupant shall apply for water service within 48 hours after occupying the premises and failure to do so will make him liable for paying for the water consumed since the last meter reading.
(Ord. of 9-3-1991(3), § 8)
543:
Bills to customers for water and sewer service shall be mailed out on such days of each month as may be determined by the city. Failure of the water and/or sewer users to pay charges duly imposed shall result in the automatic imposition of the following penalties:
(1) Nonpayment within 20 days of the due date (the 20th day of the month) will be subject to a penalty of ten percent of the delinquent account.
(2) Nonpayment within 31 days of the due date or by the first day of the following month (for months with less than 31 days) will result in the water being shut off from the water user's property.
(3) Nonpayment within 31 days will allow the city, in addition to all other rights and remedies, to terminate the agreement, and in such event, the water user shall not be entitled to receive, nor the city obligated to supply, any water under the agreement.
(4) Water and sewer services shall not be reconnected until the customer's delinquent bill, including penalty, has been paid in full. Should such customer or another customer at that same address thereafter desire to be reconnected to the water and sewer system, the customer must pay a reconnection charge for water per meter or per unit in addition to the entire past due bill, including penalty, before service will be reconnected. The reconnection charge shall be as established from time to time by the city council and set forth in the schedule of fees and charges, available for examination at city hall. Service will be reconnected only during regular business hours which, for the purposes of this article, are from 9:00 a.m. until 4:00 p.m. on Monday and 9:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m. on Tuesdays, Thursdays, and Fridays. Any reconnection made other than during regular business hours shall not be performed except as is provided in subsection (5) of this section.
(5) No customer shall have the right to have services connected or reconnected other than during regular business hours. Any connection or reconnection of services at any other time shall be performed solely at the discretion of the city maintenance supervisor and only at such times as the city maintenance supervisor is willing and able to perform such services. Before the city maintenance supervisor will connect or reconnect water after hours, the customer must first pay any past due bill, including any penalty, pay the increased security deposit required in section 32-250(1), pay the normal water reconnection charge, and in addition shall pay a after-hours reconnect fee. The reconnection fees and charges shall be as established from time to time by the city council and set forth in the schedule of fees and charges, available for examination at city hall. The customer shall take said funds to city hall and drop said funds through the slot available for after-hours payment at city hall. The customer shall then verbally inform the city maintenance supervisor that he has paid all such fees prior to the city maintenance supervisor taking any steps to reconnect the water system. In the event that any part or all of the penalties, fees, and past due bill are not paid by the customer prior to the city maintenance supervisor reconnecting the system, then the city maintenance supervisor shall as soon as possible thereafter again disconnect the water system to said customer; and an additional penalty as set by the city council shall be incurred for this action, and the additional reconnect fees and all other penalties and charges shall be charged again before the system can be reconnected.
(Ord. of 9-3-1991(3), § 9; Ord. No. 95-4, § B—D, 7-10-1995)
544:
When water and sewer service are discontinued and all bills paid, the security deposit shall be refunded to the consumer by the city.
(1) If service is disconnected for nonpayment of bills, then a security deposit in double the amount previously required shall be paid to the city in order to have services reconnected. In the event that the security deposit has not been applied to the past due bill as hereinafter provided, then a security deposit equal to that already held by the city must be paid by the customer to have its services reconnected. This must be paid in addition to all other service charges and penalties before service can be reconnected.
(2) Upon discontinuance of service for nonpayment of bills, the security deposit will be applied first towards the payment of any penalty and other fees as provided for herein; and the balance, if any, shall be applied towards the past due account. Any balance will be refunded to the consumer. If the security deposit is insufficient to cover the bill, the city may proceed to collect the balance in the usual way provided by law for the collection of debts.
(3) The city reserves the right to discontinue its service without notice for the following additional reasons:
a. To prevent fraud or abuse.
b. Consumer's willful disregard of the city's rules.
c. Emergency repairs.
d. Insufficiency of water supply due to circumstances beyond the city's control.
e. Legal processes.
f. Direction of public authorities.
g. Strikes, riots, fire, flood, unavoidable accidents.
(4) Should any individual or person cut a lock off any water meter placed thereon by the city or in any other way take action to restore service to a system without the same being performed by the city maintenance supervisor or some other person working for the city, said person shall be guilty of a misdemeanor violation of this article and additionally shall pay for all damages.
(5) Any individual who pays a water meter deposit to obtain water services to a location and if on said system the lock is cut off any water meter that has been placed thereon by the city or in any other way service is restored to said location without the same being performed by the city maintenance supervisor or some other person working for the city and the effect is that said location receive waters and said individual fails to report the same to the city within 24 hours shall also be guilty of a misdemeanor and shall additionally be responsible for all damages.
(6) The city shall have the right to remove any water meter from any location that has had the city's lock removed or in any other way said location has had water services restored to a system that has been cut off by the city. Such action shall not affect or relieve any misdemeanor violations that may have occurred related to such water service. Once a water meter is removed, before water services shall be restored to such a system, the applicant will be required to pay a reinstatement fee, or the then-required fee as set by the city, whichever amount is greater, as well as all unpaid balances owed at that location.
(7) Should the city shut off services to a particular location, or should any person develop any scheme to obtain water from the city's system without paying the city for such services, then before service may be reinstated to that location, the applicant must pay a fee equal to double the amount that would have been charged by the city had said water been obtained legally. such estimate shall be determined in any reasonable way by the city clerk including, but not limited to, using the amount of water that was used in previous bills prior to service being discontinued by the city, determining a per day rate, and then multiplying said rate times the number of days for which the city believes that water was obtained illegally.
(Ord. of 9-3-1991(3), § 10; Ord. No. 95-4, § E, F, 7-10-1995; Ord. of 8-2-2004, § 2—4)
545:
If the consumer believes his bill to be in error, he shall present his claim, in person, at the city hall before the bill becomes delinquent. Such claim, if made after the bill has become delinquent, shall not be effective in preventing discontinuance of service as heretofore provided. The consumer may pay such bill under protest and said payment shall not prejudice his claim.
(1) The city will make a special water meter reading at the request of a consumer for a fee amounting to the actual expenses incurred in making such a special meter reading, provided, however, that if such special reading discloses that the meter was over-read, no charge will be made.
(2) Water meters will be tested at the request of the consumer upon payment to the city of the actual costs of making the test, provided, however, that if the meter is found to over-register beyond three percent of the correct volume, no charge will be made.
(3) If the seal of a meter is broken by other than the city's authorized representative or if the meter fails to register correctly or is stopped for any cause, the consumer shall pay an amount estimated from the record of his previous bills and/or from other proper data.
(Ord. of 9-3-1991(3), § 11)
548: This regulation shall be known and may be cited as the "Digging of Wells Ordinance."
549: This article shall govern the rights of all citizens of the city regarding the digging of wells.
550: This article regarding the digging of wells is imposed and designed only for the protection of the public health, safety, and welfare of the citizens and to prevent any abuse and loss of public funds unnecessarily.
551:
Any person shall, prior to the digging of any well for water in the city, first make application to the council giving the location of the proposed well.
(Ord. of 5-6-1968, § I)
552:
Upon making application there shall be paid by any person desiring to dig a well a permit fee, which in the event the application is not approved will be returned. Such fee shall be as established from time to time by the city council and set forth in the schedule of fees and charges, available for examination at city hall.
(Ord. of 5-6-1968, § II)
553:
Upon application being made, in the event the council determines after investigation that the proposed well will not serve to diminish the supply of water of the water system of the city and will not interfere with or harm the water system of the city, a permit shall be issued to the applicant upon instructions from the city council by the city clerk.
(Ord. of 5-6-1968, § III)
554:
In the event a permit is issued, a well is dug and water is pumped or taken from such well, the city, in cooperation with the state health and water agencies, each month shall test the water from such well in order to determine if it is wholesome and fit for human consumption. The owner of the well shall pay each month while the well is in operation a fee, as established from time to time by the city council and set forth in the schedule of fees and charges, to the city for such testing.
(Ord. of 5-6-1968, § IV)
555:
In the event the owner of such well refuses to allow such tests to be made, refuses to pay such fee for the testing, or refuses to the city access to the well in order to obtain a sample of water, then said permit will be revoked by the council and the owner of the well shall immediately cease obtaining water from same.
(Ord. of 5-6-1968, § V)
556:
(a) Any person violating the provisions of this article shall, upon conviction thereof, be fined in accordance with section 1-8
(b) The city shall have the right to apply to the county superior court for injunctive relief in order to prevent the maintenance of a well in the city in violation of this article.
(Ord. of 5-6-1968, § VI)
559:
The following words, terms and phrases, when used in this article, shall have the meanings ascribed to them in this section, except where the context clearly indicates a different meaning:
Business using high volumes of water means city water customers using more than 10,000 gallons of water per day on average for a 12-month period.
Essential services means health care, sanitation, cooking needs, wastewater disposal, fire protection, and other essential services specified from time to time by administrative order of the mayor.
Inside city means inside of the city limits.
Low pressure means less than 20 pounds per square inch (psi).
Outdoor water usage means lawn and garden watering, noncommercial car washing, water for private swimming pools, and activities specified from time to time by administrative order of the mayor.
Outside city means outside of the city limits.
Step I restrictions means no outside water usage between the hours of 4:00 p.m. and 10:00 p.m. prevailing time on Monday through Friday, on Saturday water may be used from 12:00 noon until 10:00 p.m., and no outside water usage at any time on Sunday. The city water department must approve all use of water from the city water distribution system to fill a tank truck or to directly fill a swimming pool from a fire hydrant. The standards to be used by the water department in the exercise of this discretion shall be:
(1) To protect both storage volumes and system pressures from dropping below the levels specified in section 32-317; and
(2) To protect the water supply so that public health, safety and welfare shall not be imminently threatened.
Step II restrictions means all outdoor use of water shall be banned. Businesses using high volumes of water may be placed on significant restrictions by the mayor. The standards to be utilized by the mayor in the exercise of this discretion shall be:
(1) The effect that a high-volume user has on causing the levels specified in section 32-317
(2) Whether limiting a business's hours or days of operation will allow water levels to exceed the levels provided in section 32-317; and
(3) Any increased water supply generated by imposed restrictions, all in such manner as to best promote the public health, safety and welfare.
Step III restrictions means water shall be rationed pursuant to an administrative order issued by the mayor so as to provide for essential purposes only. Commercial and industrial users shall be restricted in accord with a plan therefore adopted by administrative order of the mayor. All outdoor use of water shall be banned.
(Ord. No. 2000-5, § 102, 8-7-2000)
560:
The purpose of this article is to provide for emergency procedures to prevent threats to public health and safety arising from periods of water shortage and drought and to prevent acts that cause, or can be reasonably expected to cause, significant imminent harm to the public health, safety and welfare or to limited water resources.
(Ord. No. 2000-5, § 100, 8-7-2000)
561:
The public shall be notified of the implementation of emergency procedures in accordance with this article and those steps which are being implemented pursuant thereto by providing notice thereof to the local news media and by posting notice thereof upon the city's bulletin board in city hall at least 24 hours prior to any implementation of emergency procedures in accordance with this article.
(Ord. No. 2000-5, § 101, 8-7-2000)
562:
Step I restrictions shall be implemented if the city exceeds 90 percent of its permitted water withdrawal amount or maximum safe production level for one day or if low pressure or loss of service is experienced. Step I restrictions shall remain in effect until all factors are relieved and shall cease upon city council determination that an adequate supply to fulfill public need exists. City council determination shall be made following recommendation of the mayor and the water superintendent and shall be subject to modification by the council at the council's next meeting. The public shall be notified of the termination of Step I restrictions through the notification thereof to local news media and by removing prior notices thereof from the city bulletin boards.
(Ord. No. 2000-5, § 103, 8-7-2000)
563:
Step II restrictions shall be implemented if Step I restrictions are not effective in restoring water levels above levels described in section 32-317. Step II restrictions shall remain in effect until factors that involved Step I restrictions are relieved for a period of two weeks following the last date on which one or more factors occurred. Upon termination of Step II restrictions, Step I restrictions shall be automatically reimplemented.
(Ord. No. 2000-5, § 104, 8-7-2000)
564:
Step III restrictions shall be implemented if Step II restrictions fail to prevent loss of water service. Step III restrictions shall remain in effect until loss of water service ceases. Upon termination of Step III restrictions, Step II restrictions shall be automatically re-implemented.
(Ord. No. 2000-5, § 105, 8-7-2000)
565:
(a) In extreme cases of loss of service the mayor may authorize the closing of valves in the water distribution system. When exercising this discretion the mayor shall:
(1) Make water available to private consumers from fire hydrants that are equipped to dispense water to the private containers of consumers;
(2) Fully consider the needs of medical facilities; and
(3) If possible, avoid the interruption of fire protection.
(b) When determining extreme cases, the mayor shall consider:
(1) Loss of service;
(2) Available water supply; and
(3) The threat posed to public health, safety and welfare by continued water usage without imposition of the restrictions authorized pursuant hereto.
(Ord. No. 2000-5, § 106, 8-7-2000)
566:
(a) For violating Step I restrictions.
(1) Private water consumers shall pay a surcharge and have the water supply terminated. Water supply shall not be restored until payment of the surcharge and of a reconnection fee for inside-city and outside-city water customers.
(2) Businesses using high volumes of water shall pay a surcharge and have the water supply terminated. Water supply shall not be restored until payment of the surcharge and of a reconnection fee for inside-city and outside-city water customers.
(3) The surcharges and reconnection fees shall be as established from time to time by the city council and set forth in the schedule of fees and charges, available for examination at city hall.
(b) For violating Step II restrictions.
(1) Private water consumers shall pay a surcharge of $200.00 and have the water supply terminated. Water supply shall not be restored until payment of the surcharge and of a reconnection fee for inside-city and out-side water customers.
(2) Business using high volumes of water shall pay a surcharge of $2,500.00 and have the water supply terminated. Water supply shall not be restored until payment of the surcharge and of a reconnection fee for inside-city and outside-city water customers.
(c) For violating Step III restrictions. Violator shall pay a surcharge of $2,500.00 and have the water supply terminated. Water supply shall not be restored until payment of the surcharge and of a reconnection fee for inside-city and outside-city water customers.
(d) Second offense violators. Any violator committing a second violation to any of the restrictions contained in subsections (a) through (c) of this section shall pay a surcharge of $2,500.00 and have the water supply terminated. Water shall not be restored until payment of the surcharge and of a reconnection fee for inside-city and outside-city water customers.
(Ord. No. 2000-5, § 107, 8-7-2000)
567:
The mayor shall have the authority to enforce the provisions of this article by discontinuance of water service in the event any person or entity violates any provisions of this article or any restrictions imposed pursuant to this article after receiving oral or written notice from the city of violations hereof.
(1) Any city employee designated by the city may terminate a service that the city employee reasonably believes to be in violation of this article.
(2) Any person whose name is on file with the city as the customer on the water account for the property where the violation occurs or originates shall be presumed to be the violator, and proof that the violation occurred on said premises shall constitute prima facie evidence that the customer committed the violation. Parents shall be presumed to be responsible for violations of their minor children, and proof that a child committed a violation on property with the parent's control shall constitute prima facie evidence that said parent committed the violation.
(3) Notwithstanding the foregoing, in any and all events that the mayor determines that a person or entity is violating or has violated any provisions of this article or any restrictions imposed pursuant to this article and that the violation endangers the public health, safety, or welfare, the mayor shall have the power and authority to immediately terminate the water service of that person.
(4) Any person aggrieved by having the water supply terminated by the mayor shall have the right to appeal the termination to the city council. Such appeal shall be taken within three days from the date of the termination by notifying the city clerk in writing specifying the grounds of appeal. The city clerk shall fix a date and time for the hearing of the appeal by the city council within two days after the receipt of the notice of appeal and, after due notice to the parties at interest, the city council shall conduct a hearing on the appeal within five days of the date the notice of appeal was received by the city clerk and proceed to decide the same within three days of the date of the hearing.
(5) In the filing of any appeal, the mayor shall have the power and authority to reinstate the water supply of the appellant, until the city council renders a decision, in order to avoid undue hardship in the event that the mayor is reasonably assured that violations for which the water supply was terminated will not continue.
(Ord. No. 2000-5, § 108, 8-7-2000)
568:
This article shall apply to all users of the city water system whether inside the city or outside the city.
(Ord. No. 2000-5, § 109, 8-7-2000)
569:
(a) All water that is pumped from aquifers by the city shall be metered by the city. Said metering shall be monitored by the city water department on a daily basis with records thereof to be maintained by the department.
(b) All water service connections to the city's water system shall be metered through an approved metering station with water consumption readings to be taken periodically by an appropriate city department.
(c) Water metering devices shall be checked for accurate calibration periodically as required and as recommended thereof.
(Ord. No. 2000-5, § 110, 8-7-2000)
570:
The mayor shall be entitled to issue rules and regulations relative to the administration of this article which are not inconsistent with the provisions of this article subject to the right of the city council to revoke or modify any such rule or regulation within 60 days following the submission thereof.
(Ord. No. 2000-5, § 111, 8-7-2000)
571:
Compliance with the provisions of this article shall not excuse or relieve any person from complying with the requirements and provisions of all other laws, ordinances, resolutions, rules and regulations applicable to water and water usage or to the conduct of any activity. Such additional laws, ordinances, rules and regulations include, but are not limited to, all applicable federal and state laws, rules and regulations and all other applicable city ordinances and resolutions.
(Ord. No. 2000-5, § 112, 8-7-2000)
572:
Each person who is a city water customer, as well as all employees, agents and servants of such water customers, shall be conclusively presumed, for purposes of this article, to have at all times complete and full knowledge of all provisions of this article.
(Ord. No. 2000-5, § 113, 8-7-2000)
573:
Any proceeding or action which may be taken with respect to the suspension or termination of water pursuant to this article shall be, and is administrative in nature with respect to the privileges of city water customers. No conviction, dismissal, acquittal, other plea or other disposition with respect to any criminal violation involving any alleged criminal conduct shall be necessary for any action pursuant to the provisions of this article or otherwise affect any action taken by the city or city officials relative thereto.
(Ord. No. 2000-5, § 113, 8-7-2000)
574:
It shall be unlawful for any person or entity to knowingly and intentionally violate any of the provisions of this article or any restrictions implemented pursuant hereto.
(Ord. No. 2000-5, § 116, 8-7-2000)
577:
(a) All residents and owners of property in the city, having need of sewerage disposal facilities in the city, are hereby required to connect to and use the sewer facilities of the city when such city facilities become available to such residents and owners of property; provided that a reasonable time, in the discretion of the mayor and council, shall be allowed after such facilities become available for connection to the facilities.
(b) After the city sewer facilities become available as herein provided, it shall be unlawful for any person owning or renting any premises in the city to permit the disposal of sewerage on any property in the city in any manner except through the city sewer system.
(c) The mayor and council shall condemn the use of all property in the city being used in violation of this article, forbidding the use of same in violation hereof, all under procedures provided by the city Charter, local health laws, state laws and other available remedies.
(Ord. of 9-3-1991(1))
580:
It shall be unlawful for anyone to dig, cut, or take any other actions in the vicinity of any water lines or sewer lines owned by the city which causes damage to any water line or sewer line or which could cause said water lines or sewer lines to become clogged, damaged, stopped up, restricted in any manner, or allow water to infiltrate the sewer system.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § A, 5-1-1995)
581:
Any person and/or their employer who shall cause any damage or restriction to any water line or sewer line owned or operated by the city, or shall cause the city water supply to be contaminated as defined by the state health code and regulations, shall be liable to the city in an amount equal to the actual cost of repairing the damage or restriction to the water line or sewer line affected by the actions of said person, any losses sustained because of any contamination, and shall further be responsible to the city and to any other persons for any other damages that they might sustain which are directly caused by such actions of said individual.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § B, 5-1-1995)
582:
Before using any type of mechanized equipment on or near any sewer line or water line owned by the city, said individual or the individual's employer must give notice to the city at least five days prior to any such work or mechanized equipment being used on, over, or near any water line or sewer line of the city.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § C, 5-1-1995)
583:
The city shall make all repairs to its water lines or sewer lines, and no individual or entity shall undertake to make any such repairs without the specific authorization and direction of the city. The city or its representatives shall make all such repairs and shall bill any violator according to the actual cost incurred, plus a reasonable amount for any time spent by city employees repairing the damage.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § D, 5-1-1995)
584:
The following shall be considered misdemeanor offenses under the city's criminal laws, and the violation of any of these provisions shall be punished in accordance with section 1-8:
(1) Using mechanized equipment on, over, or near any water line or sewer line owned or controlled by the city without first obtaining a permit to do such work from the city at least five days in advance of beginning said work.
(2) Hitting, striking, cutting, or in any harmful way damaging any water line or sewer line owned or controlled by the city.
(3) Failing to give the city notice of any digging or other work on or near the water lines or sewer lines owned or controlled by the city without first obtaining a permit and giving written notice of the intention to do such work within at least five days and no more than 30 days prior to beginning said work.
(4) Hooking up to a water system or sewer system without paying a sewer tap fee or water installation fee.
(5) Connecting personal property water or sewer lines to the city system. All such hookups must be done by city employees or authorized personnel contacted by the city.
(Ord. No. 95-2, § E, 5-1-1995)
587:
(a) The city hereby requires due compensation of three percent of the actual recurring local service revenues, as defined in O.C.G.A. § 46-5-1(b)(8) and (9); provided, however, that any company which pays in excess of three percent of the actual recurring local service revenues pursuant to an existing franchise agreement shall continue to pay in accordance with the agreement until the expiration of the franchise agreement or December 31, 2012, whichever occurs first; and any company which pays in excess of three percent of the actual recurring local service revenues in accordance with an occupational license tax arrangement shall continue to pay in accordance with such payment schedule until December 31, 2012.
(b) Regarding any telephone company that does not have retail, end user customers located within the city's municipal boundaries, the payment by such company to a municipal authority in accordance with the rates set by regulations promulgated by the department of transportation for the use of its rights-of-way shall be considered the payment of due compensation.
(Ord. No. 2009-02, § 2, 12-7-2009)
588:
The city clerk shall, on behalf of the city, exercise day-to-day administrative duties necessary to fulfill the regulatory authority of the city under O.C.G.A. § 46-5-1 et seq., and shall perform the following duties:
(1) Review application information submitted by a telephone company to the city and, if an application is incomplete, notify the telegraph or telephone company within 15 business days of the receipt of such application, identifying in such notice all application deficiencies.
(2) Report the receipt of a completed application to the council within 60 calendar days of the receipt of such completed application.
(3) Review payments of due compensation submitted by the company to ensure compliance with the provisions of the amended law and this article.
(4) Provide a coordinated function between a telephone company and all city departments on any matter relating to the amended law and this article.
(5) Arrange and evaluate, no more than once a year, a comprehensive review of the records of a company which is reasonably related to the calculation and payment of due compensation.
(6) Provide to all telephone companies located in its rights-of-way written notice of annexations and changes in municipal corporate boundaries.
(Ord. No. 2009-02, § 3, 12-7-2009)
589:
The preamble to the ordinance from which this article is derived is hereby incorporated as if fully set forth in this article.
(Ord. No. 2009-02, § 4, 12-7-2009)

592: The City Council of the City of Ty Ty, Georgia, under the authority of Article IX, Section II, Paragraphs II and IV of the Constitution of the State of Georgia and the amendments thereto, hereby ordains and enacts into law the following sections.
593: This ordinance shall be known and may be cited as the "Zoning Ordinance for the City of Ty Ty, Georgia."
594: This ordinance shall govern the use of all land and the developments thereof within the corporate limits of the City of Ty Ty, Georgia.
595: The purpose of this ordinance shall be to promote the proper location, height, bulk, number of stories and size of open spaces, the density and distribution of population, and the uses of buildings, structures, and land for trade, industry, residence, recreation, agriculture, forestry, conservation, sanitation, protection against floods, public activities, and other purposes so as to lessen congestion in the streets; to secure safety from fire, panic, and other dangers; to promote the public health and the general welfare; to provide adequate light and air; to prevent the overcrowding of land; to avoid undue concentration of population [and] to prevent urban sprawl; to facilitate the adequate provision of transportation, water, sewerage, schools, parks, and other public requirements; to promote desirable living conditions and the sustained stability of neighborhoods; to protect property against blight and depreciation; to secure economy in governmental expenditures; to conserve the value of buildings and to encourage the most appropriate use of land, buildings, and structures throughout the City of Ty Ty, Georgia; and for other purposes.

The word "lot" includes the word "plot" or "parcel."
The word "building" includes the word "structure."
The word "shall" is always mandatory, and not merely directory.
The word "used" or "occupied" as applied to any land or building shall be construed to include the words "intended, arranged, or designed to be used or occupied."

FRONT, REAR, AND SIDE YARDS ON A LOT
661: In interpreting and applying this ordinance, the requirements contained herein are declared to be the minimum requirements necessary to carry out the purpose of this ordinance. Except as hereinafter provided, this ordinance shall not be deemed to interfere with, abrogate, annul, or otherwise affect in any manner whatsoever any easements, covenants, or otherwise agreements between parties. Whenever the provisions of this ordinance impose greater restrictions upon the use of land or buildings, or upon the height of buildings, or require a larger percentage of a lot to be left unoccupied than the provisions of other ordinances, rules, regulations or permits, or any easements, covenants or other agreements between parties, then the provisions of this ordinance shall govern.
662: No buildings, structures, or land shall be used or occupied; and no building, structure, or part thereof shall be erected, constructed, reconstructed, moved, enlarged, or structurally altered unless in conformity with the regulations of this ordinance.
663: No building or structure may be erected or use established unless upon a lot as defined by this ordinance except as provided in section 3-21.
664: Except as herein provided (see section 9-3, section 9-4, and section 9-5), there shall be no more than one principal building or structure upon any lot in any residential district.
665: No open space shall be encroached upon or reduced in any manner except in conformity to the yard, setback, off-street parking space requirements, and such other regulations required by this ordinance for the district in which such building is located. Shrubbery, driveways, retaining walls, fences, curbs, and planted buffer strips shall be interpreted not to be encroachments of yards. (See section 3-24)
666: No part of any yard, other open space, or off-street parking or loading space required in connection with any building, structure, or use by this ordinance shall be considered to be part of a required yard, or other open space, or off-street parking or loading space for any other building, structure, or use except as provided in section 7-3.
667: Except as provided in section 3-22, no lot existing at the time of passage of this ordinance shall be reduced, divided, or changed so as to produce a tract of land which does not comply with the minimum dimension or area requirements of this ordinance for the district in which it is located unless said reduction or division is necessary to provide land that is needed and accepted for public use.
668: No building, structure, service area, or required off-street parking and loading facility, except driveways, shall be permitted to encroach on public rights-of-way.
669:
Accessory buildings on residential lots, when located within a front or side yard, shall be located no closer to property lines than would be allowed for a principal building. Within a rear yard, an accessory building on a residential lot shall be located at least five feet from all rear property lines, except that in the case of corner lots, accessory buildings shall be set back from the centerline of an abutting street right-of-way a distance equal to three-fourths the front yard setback established for the zoning district in which the accessory buildings are located. In the case of a through lot (see section 3-11), accessory buildings shall conform to front yard setbacks on both streets. Accessory buildings or uses on non-residential lots shall comply with front, side, and rear yard requirements established for the zoning district in which such buildings or uses are located.
1. Accessory building on separate lot: An accessory building may be permitted, as a special exception by the city council on a separate lot from the lot of the principal building provided that: (a) the lot upon which the accessory building is to be located shall be within 400 feet of the principal use; and (b) all requirements, including use restrictions, established for the zoning district in which such accessory building is to be located shall be complied with; and (c) any structure or building erected shall meet the requirements of the Georgia State Building Code and shall be approved by the building inspector. In addition to the above requirements, the city council may require design features such as buffer strips, screening, etc., as may be found necessary to protect the purposes of this ordinance.
2. Swimming pools: Swimming pools accessory to residences or commercial uses shall be enclosed by a steel mesh security fence or other substantial building material affording equal or better access control. Said fence shall have a minimum height of four feet and shall be lockable.
3. Separation from principal use: Any accessory building of more than eight feet in height shall be located at least ten feet from the principal building.
670: No building shall be erected on a lot which does not abut an open public street.
671: In the case of a corner lot, side yard setback requirements from the centerline of the street right-of-way shall equal to 75 percent of that required for the front yard setback for the respective zoning district. On a corner lot where the main entrance into a residence is facing a side yard, it shall be permissible for purposes of this ordinance to interpret the residence to be fronting on the street other than that street which said entrance faces, and side and rear yard requirements may be provided accordingly. If a building is constructed on a through lot having frontage on two or more roads not at an intersection, a setback from each road shall be provided equal to the front yard requirement for the district in which the lot is located.
672:
On corner lots within all zoning districts, no fence, shrubbery or other obstruction to the traffic sight vision, except utility poles or light or sign standards, shall exceed a height of three feet within a triangular area formed by the intersection of the right-of-way lines of two streets or a street intersection with a railroad right-of-way line, and a diagonal line which intersects the right-of-way lines at two points, each 20 feet distance from the intersection of the right-of-way lines, or, in the case of a rounded corner, from the point of intersection of their tangents; provided, however, signs, lights, or similar objects which are totally located at least 12 feet above the finished grade shall be permitted. (See illustration, page 12 [following this subsection].)
VISIBILITY AT INTERSECTIONS (See section 3-12.)
673: If either a use or class of use is not specifically indicated as being permitted in a district, either as a matter of right, or as a special exception, then such use, class of use, or structures for such uses, shall be prohibited in such district.
674:
Fallout and/or storm shelters are permitted as principal or accessory uses in any district, subject to the yard requirements of the district. Shelters shall be maintained so as not to become a hazard or blight to the community.
The city council may permit, as a special exception, construction of joint shelters by two or more property owners. Where such joint shelters are permitted, the city council may waive the side and rear yard setback requirements on the property or properties directly involved in order to permit practical and efficient location and construction; provided, however, that side and rear yard requirements shall be met where property involved in a joint proposal abuts or adjoins property not included in the proposal.
675: In the event that a district boundary line on the zoning map divides a lot of record held in one ownership on the date of passage of this ordinance, each part of the lot so divided shall be used in conformity with the regulations established by this ordinance for the district in which such parcel is located; except, however, that if the property owner of such a lot so desires, he may extend a use allowed on either portion of said lot 50 feet beyond the district boundary line in accordance with setbacks and yard requirements of the district into which he is encroaching.
676: Within any residential district, no wall or fence shall exceed eight feet in height within or along a boundary of a rear or side yard. Within the front yard, all fences shall have a height limit of four feet.
677: In an N-C, GB, WLI, and HI zoning district, where a lot abuts any residential district, a six foot wide buffer the entire length of the lot abutting the residential property shall be provided with screening as specified in section 3-19. Off-street parking associated with such uses shall be governed by this same provision.
678: Any service area, loading area, refuse, or storage area between a principal building and a public street being visible from said street and lying within 150 feet of said street shall be screened from view from the public street as specified in section 3-19.
679: Wherever screening is required by this ordinance, a durable masonry wall, or solid fence and hedge of sufficient opaqueness to provide a visual blind, designed to be compatible with the character of adjoining properties, shall be provided and maintained by the owner and his successors and assigns. Such fences and walls shall be at least eight feet in height, measured from the ground along the common lot line of the adjoining properties. Hedges or comparable natural plantings shall be of such variety that an average height of at least six feet could be expected by normal growth within no later than three years from the time of planting. The owner/developer shall install the required screening prior to the issuance of the certificate of occupancy. Occupancy will not be allowed until the screening is completed as a part of the normal developmental requirements.
680: Within any non-residential district, side yards and rear yards shall not be required adjacent to railroad rights-of-way.
681: Any lot of record existing at the time of the adoption of this ordinance which has an area or a width which is less than that required by this ordinance may be used as a building site for a structure or use permitted in that zone; provided, however, that the same yard, setback, open space, and other dimensional requirements are met that would be required for a standard lot, except as stipulated in section 3-25.
682: When a building is proposed on a lot and when on either or both lots which adjoin such lot at the street right-of-way line there exists a principal building which does not conform to the setback requirements of this ordinance, the required setback for such building shall be as follows: (1) where only one said adjoining lot contains a principal building with a non-conforming setback, the setback shall be the computed average of (a) the normal setback requirement with (b) the non-conforming setback, or (2) where both adjoining lots contain a principal building each with a non-conforming setback, the minimum setback shall be the computed average of the two non-conforming setbacks.
683: The height limits of this ordinance shall not apply to a church spire, belfry, cupola, dome, or ornamental tower not intended for human occupancy, monument, water tower, observation tower, transmission tower, chimney, smoke stack, conveyor, flag pole, radio or television tower, mast or aerial, parapet wall not extending more than four feet above the roof line of the building, and necessary mechanical appurtenances.
684: Architectural features such as cornices, eaves, steps, gutters, and fire escapes may project not more than three feet beyond any required setback line, except where such projections would obstruct driveways which are or may be used for access for service and/or emergency vehicles; provided, however, that in the case of automobile service stations, motels, and similar uses which serve the motoring public, canopies shall be allowed over a driveway or walkways within the front yard not to extend from the principal building to a point any closer than 15 feet from the street right-of-way line.
685: When a lot of record has a width less than the frontage required in the district in which it is located, then the zoning administrator shall be authorized to reduce the side yard requirements for such lot; provided, however, that there shall not be less than an eight foot side yard.
686: Areas annexed to the City of Ty Ty subsequent to the adoption of this ordinance shall be subject to this ordinance as is all land area currently located in the corporate limits of the city. It is required that the annexation petition be accompanied by the petitioner's request for rezoning, and consideration of such property for initial City of Ty Ty zoning designation shall be subject to the normal amendatory requirements of this ordinance, including the normal public hearing requirements. When property is annexed into the corporate limits of the City of Ty Ty, pursuant to action of the city council, it shall be the duty of the zoning administrator to insure compliance with the provisions of this section.
687: No mobile homes, defined as units constructed prior to June 15, 1976, shall be allowed within the city limits of the City of Ty Ty. Only manufactured homes constructed to the Federal Manufactured Home Construction and Safety Standards, governed by the National Manufactured Housing Construction and Safety Standards Act of 1974, as amended, 42 USC 5401, et seq., shall be permitted within the Ty Ty corporate limits.
689:
In order that the purposes of this ordinance as defined in section 1 may be accomplished, there are hereby established within the City of Ty Ty, Georgia, zoning districts, identified as follows:
1. E-R Environmental Resource: The purpose of this district is to protect the ecologically sensitive areas of the City of Ty Ty and to limit the active development to those uses which are compatible with the natural limits of the land.
2. A-U Agricultural Use: The purpose of this district is to permit agricultural uses, to encourage the maintenance of the rural countryside, to preserve forests and other undeveloped lands away from areas of population growth, and to allow residents to retain their traditional ways of life. The preferred land use in the district is agricultural, either active in the form of crops, or passive in the form of forest management or pasture lands. The A-U district should be utilized as a land use designation where a more intensive use of the land is unlikely to occur in the near future. The requirements of the district are designed to encourage the maintenance of a rural character until more intensive development is feasible.
3. R-14 Single Family Residential: The purpose of this district is to provide single family residential areas with minimum lot sizes of 14,000 square feet, said areas being protected from the depreciating effects of small lot development and excessive density and from the encroachment of those uses which are incompatible to a desirable residential environment.
4. R-8 Residential: The purpose of this district is to provide residential areas with a minimum lot size of 8,000 square feet, said areas being protected from uses which are incompatible to a desirable residential environment.
5. M-R Multiple Residential: The purpose of this district is to provide orderly development of higher density residential areas for one, two, and multi-family dwellings, with minimum lot sizes of 6,000 square feet, said areas being protected from the encroachment of those uses which are incompatible to a desirable residential environment.
6. R-14-M Residential: The purpose of this district is to create an area that, in addition to conventional housing, allows manufactured housing as a matter of right in a conventional subdivision. Lots in this district must have a minimum of 14,000 square feet. These districts shall be protected from the encroachment of incompatible uses which are detrimental to a sound residential environment.
7. M-H-P Manufactured Housing Park: The purpose of this district is to provide for the development of property that is suitably located and planned for manufactured home park use. Property developed in this district is to remain in single ownership for rental purposes only. Manufactured housing parks shall be developed only in strict accordance with the manufacturing housing park provisions of this ordinance.
8. N-C Neighborhood Commercial District: The purpose of this district shall be to provide and protect convenient areas for neighborhood shopping facilities.
9. G-B General Business District: The purpose of this district shall be to provide for and encourage the proper grouping and development of uses which include a wide variety of sales and services that will best accommodate the needs of the city and the traveling public in order to reduce highway traffic congestion, traffic hazards, and blight along the public streets and highways of the city.
10.
